releases.title: Steadier agent cards on Home
releases.summary: Since 0.2.16: an agent keeps one Home card through a relaunch, and its last terminal picture stays visible when it returns to Live.

fixes.title: One Home card per agent
fixes.detail: An agent moving between Live, Needs you and Ready no longer leaves an older card beside its current one, including when its task title changes or a pending request outlives its pane.

fixes.title: Keep the last terminal picture
fixes.detail: When an agent returns to Live after Needs you or a replacement pane, Home keeps its last nonempty terminal picture until fresh output arrives. Pictures are kept separate for each computer.

verification.title: Checks
verification.detail: This release has not been accepted on a phone. The captain's own phone test is still required before stable publication.

The original physical-phone flashing report remains independently unverified.

releases.title: Move a conversation to another Claude account
releases.summary: Since 0.2.15: agents can move their own conversation between signed-in Claude accounts from the terminal, and lab launches refuse an unsafe Claude launcher.

features.title: Switch Claude accounts from the terminal
features.detail: An agent can see its current Claude account, list signed-in accounts and their available quota, and move its own conversation to another account without reaching for the phone. The conversation continues with the same model and permission settings.

fixes.title: Safer lab launches
fixes.detail: A lab run refuses a missing or misplaced Claude launcher target before starting, and keeps the installed launcher from updating itself during the run.

verification.title: Checks
verification.detail: Not accepted on a device. The captain's own phone test is still required before stable publication.

knownLimits: Moving a conversation opens a replacement pane; the original pane does not stay open.
Only Claude conversations can be moved between signed-in accounts.

releases.title: Home says when Tailscale is off
releases.summary: Since 0.2.14: Home no longer says there is no network when the phone is online but Tailscale is off.

fixes.title: Tailscale is off message
fixes.detail: When the phone is online but cannot reach your computer, Home now says Tailscale is off on this phone, with a button that opens Tailscale, instead of saying the device has no network.

releases.title: Images in chat, and a quicker attach
releases.summary: Since 0.2.13: pictures in a chat open full screen, a pane opens faster, and an old Herdr is called out plainly.

features.title: Images in chat
features.detail: Pictures in the chat show inline. Tap one to open it full screen.

features.title: Old Herdr warning
features.detail: If the computer runs an out-of-date Herdr, including an old one still running, the host log and Home now say so plainly.

fixes.title: Faster pane attach
fixes.detail: A pane attaches sooner when you open it.

fixes.title: Scroll-back on the narrowest phones
fixes.detail: Scrolling back in a full-screen agent pane on a narrow screen now walks the history the phone already holds.

fixes.title: Workspace names
fixes.detail: A workspace shows its Herdr label on the phone, and a worker now names only its own pane or tab.

releases.title: Truer account chips, and sending you can see
releases.summary: Since 0.2.12: each pane shows the account it is really running on, a sent prompt says so, and cloud computers are reached over SSH.

features.title: Sending feedback
features.detail: A prompt says Sending, then Sent, and reaches the pane sooner. If it does not go, it says Not sent and offers a retry.

features.title: Chat follows the app theme
features.detail: The chat view now uses the light or dark theme you picked for the app.

features.title: Linux desktop first
features.detail: The Linux desktop app is now the first desktop option, with desklink 0.5.10.

features.title: Cloud computers over SSH
features.detail: A new cloud computer is reached over SSH. It is never joined to a tailnet.

fixes.title: Account chip and Out of room banner
fixes.detail: Each pane's account chip and Out of room banner now name the account that pane's own process runs on, not the computer's default.

fixes.title: Android scroll-back
fixes.detail: Scrolling back in a terminal on Android keeps every row.

verification.detail: Not accepted on a device.

knownLimits: Update phone and computer together: the account fix lives in the computer's muxr host.

releases.title: Cloud computers join your tailnet, and roomier keys
releases.summary: Since 0.2.11: a new cloud computer opens its Tailscale sign-in page for you, and the terminal keys are easier to hit.

features.title: Cloud computer joins your tailnet
features.detail: When a new cloud computer is ready, the phone opens its Tailscale sign-in page by itself. Approve it there and the computer joins your tailnet. Sign in to Tailscale stays on the step if you want to open the page again.

fixes.title: Terminal keys
fixes.detail: Every key is a 48 dp target with space between them, so Ctrl and Shift are no longer tapped by mistake. A row wider than the screen scrolls.

fixes.title: Quick-actions button
fixes.detail: The button that opens the radial menu has its own 48 dp target and clear space from the tabs.

verification.title: Checks
verification.detail: Not accepted on a device.

releases.title: A chat view for your agents, and a simpler way around
releases.summary: Since 0.2.10: Claude and Pi agents can be read as a chat, panes switch from one full-height sheet, and adding a Claude account no longer hangs.

features.title: Chat view
features.detail: Open a Claude or Pi agent as a chat and switch back to the terminal when you want it. Tool steps show what they touched, with icons, and fold away until you open them.

features.title: Pane switcher
features.detail: Every pane in one full-height sheet, with a live card for each.

features.title: Computers in the pane menu
features.detail: See your computers and add another from one entry in the pane menu.

features.title: Moving a Claude account
features.detail: A Claude agent can move to another account of yours, and the move is reported as done once it is.

features.title: One look for choices
features.detail: Alerts and choices open in the same sheet on Android and on the web.

fixes.title: Claude pane scrolling
fixes.detail: The history of a Claude pane scrolls smoothly under your finger.

fixes.title: Agent header on a narrow screen
fixes.detail: A long task name no longer pushes the header buttons out of reach at 390 dp and narrower.

fixes.title: Adding a Claude account
fixes.detail: The sign-in tab closes once you are signed in, so adding an account ends on the account added screen instead of hanging.

fixes.title: Screen sharing
fixes.detail: When the computer's screen-sharing portal runs without the right service, the phone tells you to restart screen sharing.

verification.detail: Not accepted on a device.

knownLimits: Update phone and computer together.

releases.title: Panes open again after Herdr closes one
releases.summary: Panes open again after Herdr closes one.

features.title: Herdr link recovery
features.detail: The host restarts a stuck Herdr link by itself.

fixes.title: Panes always open
fixes.detail: A closed pane no longer blocks new ones.

verification.title: Phone upgrade
verification.detail: 0.2.9 to 0.2.10 kept pairing and settings.

releases.title: A second host no longer replaces the first
releases.summary: Since 0.2.8: opening Usage can no longer start a second host that replaces the one you are using, and muxr up fails loudly when it runs out of restarts.

features.title: Clear failure when the host cannot restart
features.detail: When the host runs out of restarts, muxr up now exits with an error instead of quietly stopping.

fixes.title: Host drop-off
fixes.detail: A second host no longer replaces the first, so the phone stops losing its computer after you open Usage.

releases.title: Steadier Claude scrolling, right pane names, a lighter host
releases.summary: Since 0.2.7: Claude panes scroll under your finger, panes carry their Herdr tab names, and the host stops reading every agent log for the Usage screen.

features.title: Instant Latest in Claude panes
features.detail: Latest in a fullscreen Claude pane lands on the newest line at once and follows new output from there.

fixes.title: Claude pane scroll
fixes.detail: A fullscreen Claude pane now scrolls with your finger, stops when you lift it, and no longer follows new output while you scroll.

fixes.title: Pane names
fixes.detail: A pane is named by its Herdr tab label, as Herdr's sidebar shows it, with the agent and its state under it. A restart no longer renames every Claude pane after its last chat topic.

fixes.title: Cloud computer sign-in
fixes.detail: While setting up a cloud computer, its sign-in page opens from the phone while it waits, and a stalled sign-in retries after ten minutes.

fixes.title: Usage report memory
fixes.detail: The computer counts usage only while the Usage screen is open, one run at a time, at low priority and off the main loop, with a 1 GB memory cap. Other screens no longer say the computer is busy after you open Usage, and the Pi tab finishes counting.

verification.title: Checks
verification.detail: Not accepted on a device.

knownLimits: Update phone and computer together.

releases.title: Prompts reach your own panes
releases.summary: Since 0.2.6: the phone can message a Claude pane you started by hand.

features.title: Send to your own panes
features.detail: Messaging a pane you started works.

fixes.title: No timeout
fixes.detail: Fixes a send failure.

verification.title: Checks
verification.detail: Not accepted on a device.

knownLimits: Update phone and computer together.

releases.title: Continue agents on another computer and set up a cloud computer
releases.summary: Since 0.2.5: continue an agent on another computer, set up a cloud computer from the phone, and see whether each computer is healthy or busy.

features.title: Continue an agent elsewhere
features.detail: Pick another computer and the agent carries on there.

features.title: Set up a cloud computer
features.detail: The phone sets up a cloud computer for you, and a retry never makes a second one.

features.title: Healthy or Busy on Home
features.detail: Home says whether each computer is healthy or busy.

fixes.title: Stalled computers recover
fixes.detail: The phone reconnects on its own after a stall.

fixes.title: Home knows when you are offline
fixes.detail: Home judges offline by whether the computer can really be reached.

verification.title: Release candidate checks
verification.detail: The signed candidate has not been accepted on a phone, Mac or iPhone.

knownLimits: Update the phone app and computer together; mixed versions were not tested.

releases.title: Shorter pairing, alerts you can answer, and a computer app
releases.summary: Since 0.2.4: pairing is shorter, with scannable codes, a first-run screen matched to your computer, and an install that reaches computers away from home. Attention alerts now carry the agent's question and can be answered from the alert. A new computer app sets up and pairs from one window. The web app installs to the home screen and works offline. Update the phone app and computer together.

features.title: Start the first agent in one tap
features.detail: Home starts the first agent in one tap. Folder-trust questions take one tap too, and the start opens in the folder you used last. No blocking notice appears over the first agent.

features.title: Answer alerts from the alert
features.detail: Attention alerts carry the agent's question, and answering from the alert clears it everywhere: the alert, the list and the counts all agree.

features.title: One shared attention count
features.detail: A single needs-you count is shared by the app, its icon and the installed web app badge, so the number matches wherever you look.

features.title: Pairing in fewer steps
features.detail: Codes scan even from small computer screens, scanning is the primary way to pair, the spoken words are read once and end on a check mark, and a phone that was closed resumes against its computer without scanning again.

features.title: Setup that fits your computer
features.detail: A phone-first Add your computer screen carries the desktop download, pasting a link connects first, the install step matches the computer in front of you, and a first phone pairs from the computer with one command and no terminal.

features.title: Away-from-home routes by default
features.detail: Setup leads with the route that works away from home, warns on home-network-only choices, and the browser-pair command offers the route switch while you are home.

features.title: A computer app on Linux
features.detail: One window runs guided setup, pairs the phone by QR or two words, starts at login and can keep the computer awake. It installs the agent runner when it is missing and reaches Ready even on computers without one.

features.title: Send any file to an agent
features.detail: Attach any file type from the phone to an agent. Attachments stay with the draft when you leave and come back, and survive a failed first prompt.

features.title: Answer permission questions on the card
features.detail: When an agent asks permission, the question arrives on the answer card and your answer goes straight back to the waiting agent.

features.title: Accounts with private areas
features.detail: Each account on the Go agent route keeps a private area, conversations move between accounts, and Go agents start on the newest Go model through the account's own setup.

features.title: Open any folder from Files
features.detail: Files opens any folder on the computer, not only agent projects, and the desktop Computer view opens agent pages.

features.title: Move an agent to another computer
features.detail: A Computers sheet switches which computer an agent runs on.

features.title: Find the agent's changes
features.detail: The header pill and the pane actions lead to what the agent changed, ready for review.

features.title: Versioned pages that work offline
features.detail: Shareable versioned pages render on the phone with an offline preview, and shared files replay only to the phone that joins.

features.title: Install the web app
features.detail: Install the web app to the home screen from a browser tab, with its own badge, a themed launch screen and an offline shell for the next cold start.

features.title: The computer on iPhone
features.detail: The native iPhone app shows the computer desktop and drives the simulator from the phone.

features.title: Terminals that fit the screen
features.detail: Terminals taller than their box pan to every row and render whole rows; the key row fits the screen width so the arrows stay on it.

features.title: Plain connection words
features.detail: The connection screen names transports in plain words, an unreachable computer says what to try next, and a version mismatch is one quiet Home line.

features.title: SSH you can verify
features.detail: An in-app dialog asks you to confirm the computer's fingerprint before signing in, and key login works on Android.

features.title: A fresh start-agent flow
features.detail: Starting an agent guides with installed-agent readiness, keeps your own default choice, and names started agents by their kind instead of an id.

features.title: Spaces you arrange
features.detail: Reorder spaces by hand, mark favourites per agent, and pins stay scoped to each paired computer.

fixes.title: Pairing words stay whole
fixes.detail: Pairing and first-run words stay whole at the largest text, first-run content clears the status bar, and the install command wraps instead of cutting off.

fixes.title: Pasted links connect
fixes.detail: A pasted link pairs instead of reading cut off, and browser pairing over secure links works again.

fixes.title: Codes that last
fixes.detail: Pairing codes stop running out before they connect, approval is asked again after Enter, and a bad code tells the truth.

fixes.title: First prompts arrive once
fixes.detail: The first Home prompt arrives once the new agent is ready, stays ordered and restored when delivery fails, and a stalled first prompt is cleared before the app reports it not sent.

fixes.title: Terminals recover by themselves
fixes.detail: Terminal panes recover after the link or host drops, leftover modes from a crashed agent are reset, and returning from a long background marks the terminal stale at once.

fixes.title: Nothing hides under the keyboard
fixes.detail: The diff view, pane actions, the changes review, option sheets and the new-agent fields stay clear of the keyboard and the Start button at narrow widths and large text.

fixes.title: Whole text at the largest size
fixes.detail: Header titles wrap to two lines, Accounts and New agent rows read whole, the computer name shortens with an ellipsis, and tiles, sheets, notices and terminal chips stop clipping at the largest text.

fixes.title: Dictation hears speech only
fixes.detail: Non-speech labels never reach the draft, dictation waits for real speech, the meter answers quiet distant speech, and each turn carries its own context.

fixes.title: Smooth scrolling on tablets
fixes.detail: Long agent output scrolls smoothly and the Latest button works on tablets.

fixes.title: Quiet iPhone typing
fixes.detail: Smart punctuation stops rewriting terminal input, and the iPhone edit menu offers read-only copy actions.

fixes.title: Faster cold starts
fixes.detail: The installed web app starts faster: heavy viewers and payloads stay out of the cold path, and the diff highlights every language again.

fixes.title: Only the joiner sees the replay
fixes.detail: A joining phone replays only its own stream, view-only links send no input, and each change publishes one update.

fixes.title: Honest empty states
fixes.detail: A Live preview with nothing to show says so, unknown previews keep their view up, and computers with no agents say so on both ends.

fixes.title: No modal over the first agent
fixes.detail: Setup notices never cover the first agent, and the consent card stops paying the status bar twice.

fixes.title: Accounts read clearly
fixes.detail: Same-name account rows lead with what tells them apart, the added notice names accounts as the list does, sign-in lands on Accounts, and a start says which account it lands on.

fixes.title: Usage numbers stay whole
fixes.detail: Quota figures lead with the window and wrap whole, a failed activity scan retries on refresh, and plan costs are stated before you commit.

fixes.title: Moves end on a working terminal
fixes.detail: Moving a running agent, or a start that finds the agent out of room, ends on a working terminal with the situation stated.

fixes.title: Screen share asks again
fixes.detail: A restored screen share that shows nothing asks to share again instead of staying blank.

fixes.title: Shorter setup wizard
fixes.detail: First-run setup is route, review and Start; the command comes before the scan, and notifications are explained before they are asked for.

fixes.title: Setup outside a terminal
fixes.detail: Setup and pairing work without a terminal, stop re-minting codes, and reach the shared guard on computers and CI alike.

fixes.title: Names, not ids
fixes.detail: Started agents and devices are named by kind and device, never by launch ids.

verification.title: Desktop engine release prerequisite
verification.detail: npm serves the pinned desktop host 0.5.3 with its Linux and Mac engine packages, as checked during preparation. This checks availability, not desktop behaviour on the release candidate.

verification.title: Automated checks on the release candidate
verification.detail: The full suite and signed Android and computer candidate build had not run for this version when these notes were written. Checks on the individual changes are not acceptance of the combined release.

verification.title: Mac and iPhone acceptance
verification.detail: The combined candidate has not been run on a Mac host with an iPhone.

verification.title: Real-phone voice and dictation
verification.detail: Realtime voice and dictation on a real phone have not been checked for this candidate.

verification.title: Android acceptance
verification.detail: The exact signed candidate has not been installed or accepted on an Android phone or emulator.

knownLimits: Update the phone app and computer together: new phone features (file attach, folder opening, permission answers, offline pages) depend on the new computer, and mixed versions were not tested. Install the phone candidate first, then update the computer before reconnecting.
Voice can take a moment to connect when it starts.
The computer app on Linux is new: it sets up and pairs from one window, and the signed Mac build follows.
A self-hosted computer and relay are required.

releases.title: iPhone and Mac polish, Files from the terminal, and voice on BYOKit
releases.summary: Folder suggestions and dialogs stay above the iPhone keyboard, tapped paths open in Files, the iPhone app can connect over SSH, and voice, dictation and usage now run on BYOKit. Update the phone app and computer together.

features.title: Open tapped paths in Files
features.detail: Tap a file or folder path in the terminal and choose Open: folders open at their location in Files and files open previewed in their folder, on iPhone, Android and web.

features.title: SSH connection on iPhone
features.detail: The native iPhone app can pair and connect through an SSH tunnel, as Android already could.

features.title: Voice runs on BYOKit
features.detail: Realtime voice on the phone and the computer now runs on the shared BYOKit realtime library, and the Codex sign-in check comes from the same library. A simple request to ask or tell one named agent something goes straight to that agent without a planning step, and agent stop reports arrive sooner.

features.title: Dictation runs on BYOKit
features.detail: On-device dictation now runs on the shared BYOKit dictation library with settings chosen from measured runs: English is used directly, the whole recording is read again when you stop so missed words come back, and the last words spoken before stopping are kept.

features.title: Agent status chips on Android
features.detail: On Android, busy, attention and voice status chips use the shared BYOKit status bar library.

features.title: Smoother first run
features.detail: Setup on the computer shows each connection route with its requirements and one recommendation. On the phone, pairing opens the scanner directly, shows one consent screen and the matching words, then opens Home. In the browser, the first-run screen tells you to paste the pairing link instead of scanning a QR code.

fixes.title: Folder suggestions while typing
fixes.detail: The project folder field and its suggestions stay visible above the keyboard, match folder names regardless of case (Documents on a Mac), include linked folders, keep focus while you browse, and show a ~/project example on any computer.

fixes.title: Keyboard on iPhone
fixes.detail: The pairing dialog and terminal link actions stay clear of the keyboard, Safari no longer zooms in on a focused field, and the page lines up again after the keyboard closes.

fixes.title: Photos on iPhone
fixes.detail: Choosing a photo in Safari or the installed web app attaches it instead of failing.

fixes.title: Files while an agent starts
fixes.detail: Opening Files while an agent is still starting shows a waiting state and then loads, instead of an Unknown session error.

fixes.title: Option sheets on Android
fixes.detail: On Android, option sheets move above the keyboard instead of being covered by it.

fixes.title: Tapped paths and links
fixes.detail: Tapping a file path in the terminal shows Copy, Insert and Open actions as web links already did.

fixes.title: Web terminal reopens by itself
fixes.detail: Reopening the web app onto a terminal reconnects without tapping Retry when the link was not ready yet.

fixes.title: Default agent is one you have
fixes.detail: The Home dock no longer picks Pi when the computer does not have it installed; a choice you made yourself is kept.

fixes.title: Paths from your home folder
fixes.detail: A path like ~/project or project starts agents, lists folders and runs commands from your home folder.

fixes.title: Agent start errors
fixes.detail: When an agent cannot start, the phone says why and offers Back to Home instead of waiting silently.

fixes.title: Usage readings
fixes.detail: Codex, OpenCode Go and Z.ai plan limits come from the shared BYOKit usage library and stay separate per account.

fixes.title: Plugins no longer cut off voice
fixes.detail: Enabling, updating or disabling a plugin no longer ends an active voice call. Plugin-declared computer streams are retired.

fixes.title: Updated libraries
fixes.detail: The computer uses desklink 0.3 (adding macOS Apple silicon desktop support), the accounts library 0.9 with single-use refresh protection, and newer link, relay and Herdr libraries. Codex status checks no longer hold up other requests.

verification.title: Desktop engine release prerequisite
verification.detail: npm serves the pinned @desklink/host 0.3.0 with its Linux x64 and macOS arm64 engine packages, as checked during preparation. This checks availability, not desktop behaviour on the release candidate.

verification.title: Automated checks on the release candidate
verification.detail: The full suite and signed Android/npm candidate build had not run for this version when these notes were written. Checks on the individual changes are not acceptance of the combined release.

verification.title: Mac and iPhone acceptance
verification.detail: Some iPhone and Mac fixes (photo attach, Files while an agent starts, web keyboard layout, home paths, web terminal reopen, pairing dialog, folder placeholder, path Open, default agent) were checked on a private Mac host with an iPhone simulator before they merged. Others, including iPhone SSH, folder suggestions above the keyboard and terminal link actions, were not run on a Mac or iPhone. The combined candidate has not yet been run on a Mac host with an iPhone.

verification.title: Real-phone dictation and voice
verification.detail: Dictation settings were chosen from recorded-speech measurements and an emulator; dictation and realtime voice on a real phone have not been checked for this candidate.

verification.title: Android acceptance
verification.detail: The exact signed candidate has not been installed or accepted on an Android phone or emulator.

knownLimits: Update the phone app and computer together: several new phone features (opening tapped paths, home-relative and linked folders, photo attach in Safari, voice on BYOKit) depend on the new computer, and mixed versions were not tested. Install the phone candidate first, then update the computer before reconnecting.
Voice can take a moment to connect when it starts; connecting ahead of time waits on a BYOKit fix.
Files browses only the projects your agents have open: a tapped folder outside them shows Not in Files (a file outside them opens in the file viewer).
A self-hosted computer and relay are required. Native iPhone desktop viewing is not available yet; open Computer in the web app on iPhone.
Transient blank terminal frames around an explicit keyboard resize remain a known limitation.
This is a candidate for acceptance. npm latest and Play production are not updated by building it; a successful build does not prove phone, microphone or desktop behaviour.

releases.title: Choose your accounts, watch your agents, and send files
releases.summary: Pick a subscription account for each agent, add or sign in to accounts from the phone, browse files and send prompt attachments, and watch an agent’s browser or emulator live. Update the phone app and computer together.

features.title: Choose and manage subscription accounts
features.detail: Pick an account when starting an agent, or let Auto pick the signed-in account with the most room left. Add an account, sign in again, rename it, and move a running conversation to another account from the phone.

features.title: Files and prompt attachments built in
features.detail: Browse the agent’s files and send files with a prompt through muxr’s built-in controls.

features.title: Watch an agent’s browser or emulator
features.detail: Open a live view from the session header when an agent is using a browser or Android emulator, and take control when needed.

features.title: Terminal colours and pane map
features.detail: Tune terminal colours in Settings and open a map of the session’s panes from its header.

features.title: Tasks and usage at a glance
features.detail: Agent rows lead with the task, Spaces shows live agent counts, and each provider’s Usage tab shows token counts and trends.

features.title: A private link to your computer
features.detail: Pair with a computer and relay you or someone you trust operates. Confirm the matching words before approving the encrypted link; no muxr-operated account service or relay is required.

features.title: Guided setup after installation
features.detail: Installing muxr on the computer opens guided setup directly, so you can connect your phone without finding a separate setup command.

features.title: Replace your computer’s pairing keys
features.detail: If your self-hosted computer’s keys were exposed, replace them with muxr devices rotate-keys --unpair-all. Every device must pair again once after rotating, and inbound computer collaborations must be set up again.

features.title: Check agent sign-in readiness
features.detail: The computer reports whether supported agents are installed and signed in, with hints for installing or signing in when needed.

features.title: Private agent alerts
features.detail: Agent lifecycle alerts keep task titles encrypted through the relay. Tapping an alert opens its agent on the right computer; if another computer is selected, Settings opens so you can select the one that sent it.

fixes.title: Codex agents open from the herd
fixes.detail: Codex panes reported by Herdr now appear as agents you can open, even when Herdr has not attached conversation metadata.

fixes.title: Codex Voice uses your accounts
fixes.detail: Codex Voice planning uses the subscription accounts configured on the computer.

fixes.title: Healthy links stop saying Connecting
fixes.detail: The phone no longer shows a spurious Connecting state while its link is healthy. Pairing and version mismatches also explain what needs attention.

fixes.title: Scroll and return to the latest output
fixes.detail: Claude Code follows your finger when you drag or fling. Latest returns to the bottom for every agent kind on Android and web, including while output is streaming.

fixes.title: Clearer errors and desktop controls
fixes.detail: Computer request failures show a useful reason, and the desktop key row includes Alt, Super and the other desktop keys. Screen-sharing approval and capture recovery are steadier.

fixes.title: Correct app icons
fixes.detail: Native and web builds use the corrected muxr icons.

fixes.title: Updated connection and agent libraries
fixes.detail: The computer uses the updated Herdr and link libraries for prompts, reads and waits, and removing a paired device clears its relay subscriptions and preserves the revocation.

fixes.title: Terminal links and custom paths on iOS
fixes.detail: Tapping a terminal link on iOS opens the open-link popup, and the custom project path picker stays visible above the keyboard so you can select your path.

verification.title: Desktop engine release prerequisite
verification.detail: npm serves the pinned @desklink/host 0.2.0 and Linux x64 engine package, as checked during preparation. This checks availability, not desktop behaviour on the release candidate.

verification.title: Automated checks on the release candidate
verification.detail: The full suite and signed Android/npm candidate build have not been run for this version during changelog preparation. Earlier checks on individual changes are not acceptance of the combined release.

verification.title: Phone and emulator acceptance
verification.detail: The exact signed candidate has not been installed or accepted on a phone or emulator. The installed phone app’s signer still needs comparison with the candidate before choosing direct APK or Play Internal delivery.

verification.detail: No iOS simulator, device or store build acceptance is recorded for this version.

features.title: Terminal colours and pane map

features.title: Every agent leads with its task

fixes.title: Claude Code panes scroll

fixes.title: Clearer computer errors

features.title: Rename agents, tabs, panes and spaces
features.detail: Long-press an agent, tab, pane or space and choose Rename. The new name is saved on your computer, so every device and the desk see it, and automatic naming leaves it alone. If a name cannot be used, the app says why.

fixes.title: Right now stays current

fixes.title: Quick actions stay while you type

releases.title: Your computer, your terminals, your voice
releases.summary: Open your computer's screen from the phone, work terminals by tab and pane, dictate as you speak, and see plan limits at a glance. This is the first stable release since 0.1.25, so it also includes every change from 0.1.26 to 0.1.28.

features.title: Your computer's screen on your phone
features.detail: Open Computer from any terminal to see and control the desktop. Tap to take control, the pointer follows your finger, a key row and clipboard work both ways, and the phone turns to landscape while you use it. It works over your local network, your private mesh or a direct SSH connection.

features.title: Approve screen sharing once
features.detail: The computer asks for screen-sharing permission once, during setup or pairing, and remembers it, so opening Computer later does not wait on a prompt.

features.title: A screen for servers that have none
features.detail: On a server with no display, muxr starts a private one when you open Computer and keeps other accounts off it.

features.title: Tabs and panes, the way your desk has them
features.detail: The row above the composer lists the workspace's tabs, and + opens a new one that attaches on the first try. The header counts the tab's panes, so you can step between them or split a new one.

features.title: Panes as a live tree
features.detail: Panes shows every tab and agent as a live tree with names, tasks and status, and the pane sheet mirrors the real split on your computer.

features.title: Dictation that writes as you speak
features.detail: Words appear in the composer while you talk, on the terminal and on Home. Pick a language, download a model when you need one, and teach it your own word replacements.

features.title: Right now, at a glance
features.detail: A small strip above Live shows how much of each connected plan is left and when it resets, with the computer's memory, disk and load beside it. Figures stay put through slow or failed reads.

features.title: Agents go by their names
features.detail: Every surface leads with the agent's name and puts its task underneath. Agents can name their own workspace and pane with muxr name.

features.title: Live leads with what needs you
features.detail: Home's Live row shows agents that need you first, then working ones, in a steady order. Finished results stay visible until you open them.

features.title: Seamless agent switching and gestures
features.detail: Swipe between agents in one continuous pager. Gestures in Settings shows what each swipe, pinch and long-press does and lets you change it.

features.title: A rebuilt terminal composer
features.detail: One header, a composer rail and radial quick controls. Edit the key row and add your own keys, send quick replies in one tap, reuse history safely and paste in one tap.

features.title: Answer prompts with a tap
features.detail: When an agent asks a question in the terminal, tap an answer. Other typing is held back while the prompt waits, so a stray key cannot answer it.

features.title: Links you can trust
features.detail: Web links printed in the terminal open safely, and a long-press copies them.

features.title: Shared artifacts, kept
features.detail: Files your agents share gather in one timeline per session. Large files download progressively and resume after a dropped connection, and old history is cleared on a schedule.

features.title: More ways to connect
features.detail: Choose a connection route before pairing, connect over direct SSH, and install your phone's SSH key on the computer from the app. Paired Android phones find the computer again on the local network.

features.title: Install the web app
features.detail: The web app installs as a standalone app, keeps a personal browser paired for 30 days and can receive notifications without an account.

features.title: Guided setup
features.detail: muxr setup walks you through the choices in the terminal and writes them to a config file you or an agent can edit and apply again.

features.title: Home opens instantly
features.detail: Home opens from its last saved state, works offline and reconnects to your computer on its own.

features.title: Near-black dark mode
features.detail: Dark surfaces are now near-black and seamless, with the previous raised look still available in Appearance. Settings show a preview of each choice, and document previews open in your current theme.

features.title: Voice engines explained
features.detail: Settings explains each voice engine and lets you try it, and realtime voice finds and works your agents more reliably.

fixes.title: Faster everywhere
fixes.detail: Cold launch, opening a pane, reconnecting and typing are all quicker, and Android terminal output scrolls smoothly.

fixes.title: Back always goes Home
fixes.detail: Going back from an agent always returns to Home.

fixes.title: A lost connection no longer ends the terminal
fixes.detail: If the computer drops out, the terminal reconnects with a bounded backoff and says what it is doing instead of closing.

fixes.title: Agents started at the desk show up
fixes.detail: Agents you start at the computer appear on Home without restarting anything.

fixes.title: No duplicate alerts
fixes.detail: The agent you are looking at no longer alerts you about itself.

fixes.title: Composer fits short screens
fixes.detail: The composer follows the keyboard, and Home's composer stays usable on short phones.

fixes.title: Voice failures in plain words
fixes.detail: A failed voice call says what went wrong instead of showing a raw error.

fixes.title: Jump to latest works everywhere
fixes.detail: Jump to latest means the same thing in every terminal, and a message sent to a plain shell goes through.

releases.title: Steadier terminals, honest usage
releases.summary: Terminal graphics settle sharp instead of flickering, a dropped host reconnects instead of ending your session, and Usage reports only what the transcripts actually show.

features.detail: Tapping the terminal no longer forces the keyboard open when you only wanted to read. The shortcut is a setting, and it stays hidden on web where it has no meaning.

features.title: Visual release notes

fixes.title: Terminal images settle sharp

releases.title: Computers that work together
releases.summary: Authorize paired computers to read, watch, and prompt one another safely.

features.title: Cross-computer agent access
features.detail: Agents list sessions, read output and status, watch completion, and send prompts across allowed computers without shell or destructive access.

features.title: Saved computers in Settings
features.detail: Select paired computers in Settings and see saved computers immediately while live collaboration checks finish.

features.title: Compact public agent guide
features.detail: Load the compact public agent guide with muxr --skill, pull focused topics on demand, and read bounded host history with muxr diagnostics; setup and updates never rewrite agent instructions.

fixes.title: Voice stays on one machine
fixes.detail: Native realtime voice remains pinned to the machine running it while it works with allowed agents elsewhere.

legacyEntries.title: Pairing that stays paired
legacyEntries.summary: QRs scan reliably, saved machines switch cleanly, and browser access survives refresh.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Scan a four-margin terminal QR directly from Settings → Pair another machine, with manual entry beside it.
- See the active computer on Home and switch saved machines there; stale sessions and forgotten computers disappear immediately.
- Show the host's real platform and only launchable agents in the Home composer.
- Pair browsers from one short two-minute HTTPS link with host-enforced control or explicit view-only access.
- Wait for browser storage to commit before setup reports success, recover interrupted grant indexes, and show an explicit recovery screen instead of silently appearing unpaired.

legacyEntries.title: One tap, one destination
legacyEntries.summary: Pairing, Usage, machine details, and Preview lose their duplicate steps.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Keep Scan QR and manual pairing separate; the manual screen now contains only the string field and Connect.
- Open the provider-tab Usage screen from one plain pill beside Machine.
- See the active transport, relay URL, and muxr CLI version in machine details.
- Preview only detected HTML frontends by page title and carry the paired relay through the tunnel.

legacyEntries.title: Pair without the payload
legacyEntries.summary: A short relay-qualified code replaces the giant native pairing string.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Enter one short two-minute pairing string or scan the same value as a QR.
- Pair through LAN, Tailscale, Cloudflare, or a custom relay without a central discovery service.
- Pairing lookups are encrypted, single-use, and deleted after resolution; completed handoffs are deleted after grant delivery.

legacyEntries.title: Polish everywhere
legacyEntries.summary: A design-review pass plus simpler, fewer bundled plugins.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Proper green/red diffs, theme-correct voice overlay, and press feedback across terminal, sheets, and plugin screens.
- Copy a link from recent terminal output in one tap from the Actions menu.
- Fewer, simpler bundled plugins: Code (files, changes, and history) and Status (usage and vitals).
- The read-only browser now shows audited read-only plugin screens like Usage and Files; bundled plugin permissions refresh once after this safety upgrade.
- The setup menu guides instead of dead-ending, pairing recovers from expired sessions, and the app names OMP correctly.

legacyEntries.title: Visual usage and steadier voice
legacyEntries.summary: Charts and progress in plugin screens, plus screen-off voice fixes.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- See today’s per-agent token activity as charts and Codex limits as progress rings on a native Usage screen.
- Build richer plugin screens with data-bound progress, responsive columns, and bounded bar/ring charts — the same public UI vocabulary every extension uses.
- Keep voice alive with the screen off: wake and Wi-Fi locks during calls, speaking counts as activity, and reconnects recover over long sessions.
- Plugin failures show one clean message instead of technical detail; Git history shows a friendly empty state when a session has no folder.

legacyEntries.title: Readable code and honest usage
legacyEntries.summary: Syntax-highlighted source and offline multi-agent activity.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Read source with line numbers and consistent syntax highlighting across Files, Markdown, plugin screens, and diffs.
- Use the same bounded code and diff views from third-party plugins without HTML or native modules.
- See today’s local coding-agent activity through a pinned offline ccusage backend, alongside current Codex limits.
- Keep costs, prompts, model names, projects, and session details out of the Usage card.

legacyEntries.title: Shared relays and safer setup
legacyEntries.summary: Guided onboarding, machine-scoped VPS relays, and runtime agent discovery.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Run `muxr` for a reviewed, Cancel-first setup and maintenance menu.
- Host one encrypted relay for several machines without copying relay-owner authority.
- Pair a read-only browser from a clickable HTTPS link with clear eight-hour expiry and recovery.
- Choose agents from the connected Herdr host and view safe coding-CLI usage status.

legacyEntries.title: muxr
legacyEntries.summary: A focused mobile control surface for coding agents running through Herdr.
legacyEntries.markdown:
- Watch sessions, terminals, changes, and attention state from your phone.
- Send keys, inspect attachments, and start agents in a selected workspace.
- Use provider-neutral realtime voice or fully local Whisper dictation.
